title: Survey reveals where most of you draw the line when it comes to AI
summary: Our reader poll put LLM trust to the test by asking whether you'd hand an agent full access to your computer.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority LLMs have only been on the scene for a few years, but for better or worse, they’ve long since escaped the chat window. Instead of just answering questions or rewriting your emails, the next wave of AI agents wants to do most of the clicking for you, but this generally requires getting its hands on much more of your computer. We can probably all agree that this could save you a lot of tedious work, but it also means handing a somewhat unpredictable machine the digital equivalent of your house keys. We wanted to know if you were cool with that. That trade-off came into focus when we tried OpenClaw earlier this year, an open-source tool that effectively lets an LLM work directly with your computer and connected services. We found it could be impressively capable when given that freedom, but we also saw how prompt injection could potentially turn the same access against you . In our OpenClaw coverage, we ran a reader poll to ask you a simple question: Would you give an LLM full access to your computer? Your response was as emphatic as it was predictable, and the results are in the pie chart below.

title: This Google AI experiment wants to become your family’s unpaid intern
summary: Remember Google CC? It's now a shared AI assistant for families.
body: TL;DR Google is expanding CC from a personal daily briefing tool into an AI assistant for families and households. Up to six people can share information with CC, which can manage shared calendars, tasks, reminders, and Daily Briefs. CC can also help with chores like filling out forms, making shopping lists, and planning meals. Late last year, Google introduced an all-new attempt at making Gemini a lot more useful for everyday life. Called CC, it was a new AI agent designed to give you a daily briefing and help you follow up on tasks by tracking information found within your Gmail, Calendar, and Drive. The Google Labs experiment evolved into Gemini’s Daily Brief , and Google is now taking the original CC concept and expanding its horizon. Google is transforming CC into an agent for families and households . Instead of only helping one person, the AI tool will take a broader household approach, complete with its own dedicated Google account.
